items.title: How Far Could RKLB Stock Fall In The Next Shock?
items.summary: Rocket Lab (RKLB) trades near $64, about 57% below the high it set inside the last year, though it is still up 49.5% over twelve months against 19.7% for the S&P 500. The business did not break along the way. What changed is the wait: how long before Neutron flies, and how much cash goes out first.

items.summary: AST SpaceMobile's shares have come back to Earth. Is it now a better buy than L3Harris Technologies?

items.title: Should You Care That Lockheed Martin's Buyback Effect Is Fading?
items.summary: Lockheed Martin (LMT) has spent the past three years handing its owners a slightly bigger slice of the company each year, and the arithmetic worked. Earnings per share grew faster than net income. The stock now sits well below its 52-week high, which makes the question worth asking again: is that quiet compounding still running at the speed the record suggests.

items.summary: RDW's phased-array investment could expand its Defense Tech reach into resilient space communications, but funded programs and returns remain unproven.

items.title: Is LUNR Worth Buying as Growth Accelerates but Valuation Stays Rich?
items.summary: Intuitive Machines' surging revenues and record backlog strengthen its growth case, but rich valuation, cash use and execution risks keep the investment setup balanced.

items.title: How Long Can Rocket Lab Stock Wait On Neutron?
items.summary: Rocket Lab (RKLB) has fallen about 49% over the past three months, while signing the biggest launch contract in its history. The risk sits in the gap between those two facts. The threat is not on the demand side. It is that the company spends far ahead of Neutron, the rocket meant to turn its cash around, and Neutron has not flown.
